questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Niger?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Niger article.

questions.proof: The capital is Niamey, and the official language is Hausa.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Niger?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Niger on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Niger article.

questions.proof: The longest border is with Nigeria to the south.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is surrounded by _____ and Libya to the north, Chad to the east, Nigeria and Benin to the south, and Burkina Faso and Mali to the west.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “surrounded”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Niger article.

questions.proof: It is surrounded by Algeria and Libya to the north, Chad to the east, Nigeria and Benin to the south, and Burkina Faso and Mali to the west.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Later _____ controlled the land that is now Niger.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Later”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Niger article.

questions.proof: Later France controlled the land that is now Niger.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “History: There was a military coup in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Niger article.

questions.proof: History: There was a military coup in 2010.
